chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Yaʿqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Shuʿayb, from Abi Kahmas, who said:

I was present at the death of Ismaʿil while Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام was seated beside him. When death came upon him, he bound his jaw, closed his eyes, and covered him with the sheet. Then he ordered that he be prepared, and when his affair was completed, he called for his shroud and wrote on the edge of the shroud:
Ismaʿil bears witness that there is no god but Allah.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: If he dies at night in a house, a lamp should be lit there until morning, and he should not be left alone. Rather, someone should remain with him remembering Allah the Exalted, reciting His Book or whatever of it he knows well, and seeking forgiveness for him.

key_terms.الْمَوْتُ: death, the moment of passing away
key_terms.الْمِلْحَفَةَ: the covering sheet placed over the deceased
key_terms.كَفَنِهِ: his shroud used for burial preparation
key_terms.لَحْيَيْهِ: his two jaws, indicating binding the mouth closed after death
key_terms.مِصْبَاحٌ: a lamp lit in the house until morning
key_terms.يَسْتَغْفِرُ: seeks forgiveness on behalf of the deceased

ai.seo_question: What should be done for a deceased person at the time of death and during the night after passing away?
ai.summary: This report describes what was done at the time of Ismaʿil’s death in the presence of Imam Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, including closing the eyes, binding the jaw, covering the deceased, and writing the shahadah on the shroud. It also includes a legal instruction from al-Shaykh that a deceased person at night should not be left alone, and that dhikr, Qur'an recitation, and seeking forgiveness should continue beside him until morning.
